text:
I've made concrete fixes and found the one structural issue that needs your input before I change it (it affects `/develop`'s documented workflow). Here's the full picture.

## Fixed now (verified: typecheck clean, 1696/1696 unit tests pass)

**1. Scheduler no longer executes PRDs from unapproved Epics** (`src/main/scheduler.cjs`, `reconcile()`)
The scheduler picked up **any** `.md` file it found under `scheduler/epics/<id>/prds/`, with zero regard for the owning Epic's approval status. A PRD sitting in a `proposed` Epic (or one dropped in a directory that was never registered via `ensureEpic` at all — i.e. written directly to disk, bypassing the app entirely) would still get executed as a `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` job. This is the core hole: the "Approve & start" human gate was cosmetic for the scheduler — approving the chat session did nothing to stop the scheduler from running PRDs that already existed on disk. Now a PRD only becomes eligible once its owning Epic is registered with `status: 'active'`.

**2. Audit trail added** (`src/main/lib/auditLog.cjs`, new)
Every Epic mint and every PRD write now appends a JSONL record to `~/.claude/session-manager/audit-log.jsonl` — timestamp, cwd, epicId/slug, status, title, and the calling process's pid/ppid/claude-session-id (best-effort; there's no cryptographic caller identity across the admin API, so this is the strongest traceability actually available). Wired into `epicMint.cjs` and `prdCreate.cjs`.

**3. The unattended feedback-sweep no longer auto-runs work** (`scripts/lib/watchdogHelpers.cjs`)
`emitFeedbackPRD` minted a brand-new **active** Epic with no human in the loop — an unattended, timer-driven path with the exact same danger as the retired `/process-feedback`/`/my-feedback` skills, just reimplemented. It now files `status: 'proposed'`, matching its sibling `rcaFeedbackHook.cjs`. (Confirmed this sweep is currently dead code — not called from the live scheduler heartbeat, per a comment at `scheduler.cjs:1330` — but it's exercised by tests and could be re-wired, so I fixed it rather than leaving a landmine.) Updated its test's assertion accordingly.

## Open structural gap — needs your decision

`scheduler_create_prd` (the MCP tool exposed to **every** Claude Code session opened in this repo, via `.mcp.json`) and its underlying `chat:create-prd` IPC both go through `prdCreate.createPrd` → `scheduler.cjs`'s `writePrd`. When the caller doesn't supply a `sourcePromptId` that resolves to an existing Epic, this **mints a brand-new Epic with `status: 'active'` immediately** — no approval gate at all, and my scheduler fix doesn't catch it because the Epic is already `active` the instant it's created.

This is the same shape of hole as the other two, but I can't fix it unilaterally: `/develop`'s **documented, human-invoked** workflow relies on exactly this behavior — SKILL.md tells the agent to call `scheduler_create_prd` directly, no separate mint step. There's no signal available at the MCP layer that distinguishes "a human just typed `/develop`" from "some other session/subagent decided on its own to call this tool" — both look identical to the tool.

Two ways to close it, and I'd like your call:
- **(a) Make ALL new-Epic-via-PRD-create land as `proposed`.** Fully closes the hole, but changes `/develop`'s UX: every batch of PRDs it generates would need a manual "Approve & start" click before anything runs, instead of running immediately.
- **(b) Leave `/develop`'s immediate-execution UX intact, but add a narrower guard** — e.g., require the caller to pass a value proving intent (not spoofable through the tool schema alone), or restrict `scheduler_create_prd`'s admin route to only fire from a chatRunner-spawned process (`SM_CHAT_SESSION_ID` present) that's *itself* already running inside an approved, active Epic. This is weaker (still local-process-trust-based) but doesn't change today's `/develop` behavior.

Let me know which direction, or if you want to just try (a) and see if it's acceptable in practice.
